learning_outcomes.text: Acquire knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling the learning of new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.

Develop the ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Mechanical Industrial Engineering.
Cultivate the ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Gain basic knowledge on the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases, and computer programs with engineering applications.
Demonstrate capacity for organization and time planning.
Develop capacity to learn and work autonomously.
Acquire capacity to apply knowledge to practice.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated by means of the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (normally within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
Students can transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Students have developed those learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Cover the need for basic knowledge in technological subjects, ensuring learning methodologies that allow students to adapt to new situations.
Be able to solve new problems encountered in multidisciplinary environments, and make appropriate decisions at all times.
Acquire basic knowledge about computer science, understand the computer, the Linux operating system, and acquire a correct programming methodology.
Generate clear, well-structured code, comprehensible by a potential code modifier, and adaptable to future needs.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1 – Introduction to Computer Science. Computer science, computer, instructions and data; Information representation; Hardware; Software; and Computer applications.
Topic 2 – Operating Systems. Definition, classification and functions; Evolution, graphical interface and command line; and GNU/Linux Operating System.
Topic 3 – Problems, algorithms and programs. Basic foundations; High and low-level languages; Programming paradigms; and Problem-solving tools.
Topic 4 – Elements of programming. Data and data types; Constants; Variables; and Expressions, Operations, Priority Rules.
Topic 5 – Structured programming. Control statements; Documentation.
Topic 8 – Basic concepts of databases. Database design and management.
Topic 9 – Implementation of databases at an office automation level.
teaching_methods: Theoretical classes (lectures) using audiovisual aids (projector, printed material)
Practical classes in the classroom (exercises on paper or with computers)
Laboratory practicals (exercises related to theoretical content using computers)
Use of virtual classroom for resources, questionnaires, and collaborative tasks
Basic informational competencies course (complementary activity with a presentation session and virtual campus work)
assessment_rules: For continuous evaluation, the final grade (CF) is obtained by the formula CF = 0.75 * CT + 0.25 * CP, where CT refers to Theory and Problem Activities and CP to Practical Activities. To pass, a final grade of at least 5 points is required, along with a minimum of 5 in the final written exam, approval of at least half of the practicals, and approval of at least 3 out of 4 questionnaires. If the overall grade is 5 or more but one of the other conditions (final exam, practicals, questionnaires) is not met, the final grade will be the minimum between 4 and the final exam grade. For single evaluation, the final grade (CF) is obtained by the formula CF = 0.75 * CT + 0.25 * CP, only if CT >= 5 and CP >= 5; otherwise, CF = min(CT, CP). Students must opt for single evaluation within one month from the start of the semester.
